title: Single-Molecule FISH Protocol for Developing Mouse Retinal Vasculature
author: Augustine, Smith, et al.

steps.title: Reconstitute probe stock
steps.instruction: Resuspend the lyophilized oligonucleotide probe mixture in TE buffer (10 mM Tris‑HCl, 1 mM EDTA, pH 8.0) to a final volume of 200 µL for custom Pecam1 Quasar 570 (5 nmol) or 40 µL for pre‑designed Gapdh Quasar 670 (1 nmol) to obtain a 25 µM probe stock; mix by pipetting up/down, vortex, briefly centrifuge, aliquot, and store at –20 °C.

steps.title: Prepare 10× PBS stock
steps.instruction: In a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube add one PBS tablet, pipette 10 mL nuclease‑free water, vortex until homogeneous, then bring the volume to 20 mL with additional nuclease‑free water.

steps.title: Prepare 2× PBS working
steps.instruction: Transfer 10 mL of the 10× PBS stock to a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube, add 40 mL nuclease‑free water, and vortex until homogeneous to make 50 mL of 2× PBS.

steps.title: Prepare 4% formaldehyde
steps.instruction: In a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube pipette 22 mL nuclease‑free water, add one 10 mL ampule of 16 % formaldehyde, then add 8 mL of 10× PBS; invert to mix thoroughly to obtain 40 mL of 4 % formaldehyde in 2× PBS. Handle in a fume hood with gloves and safety glasses.

steps.title: Prepare 1× PBS working
steps.instruction: Add 5 mL of 10× PBS to a sterile 50 mL Falcon tube, add 45 mL nuclease‑free water, and vortex until homogeneous to make 50 mL of 1× PBS.

steps.title: IB4 staining of retinas
steps.instruction: Perform washing, blocking, and labeling of retinas with isolectin‑B4 as follows:

substeps.instruction: Wash retinas three times in 1.8 mL PBS at 21 °C for 5 min each on a flat‑angle shaker.
Incubate retinas in 500 µL IB4 blocking buffer for 1 h with gentle shaking.
Add 200 µL IB4 blocking buffer containing Biotinylated IB4 (1:150) and incubate 16 h at 4 °C with gentle shaking.
Rinse retinas four times in 1.8 mL PBS at 21 °C for 15 min each on a flat‑angle shaker.
Add 200 µL IB4 blocking buffer containing Streptavidin‑Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200) and incubate 2 h at 21 °C with gentle shaking.
CRITICAL: Vortex the probe mixture thoroughly, then centrifuge 20 min at 9800 × g (21 °C) to remove aggregates; use the supernatant for incubation.
Wash retinas four times in 1.8 mL PBS at 21 °C for 15 min each on a flat‑angle shaker.

steps.title: Optional immunolabeling and IB4 staining
steps.instruction: Replace step 7 with the following immunofluorescence protocol:

substeps.instruction: Wash retinas three times in 1.8 mL PBS at 21 °C for 5 min each on a flat‑angle shaker.
Incubate retinas in 500 µL immunofluorescence blocking buffer for 2 h at 21 °C with gentle shaking.
Add 200 µL blocking buffer containing the primary antibody (desired concentration) and Biotinylated IB4 (1:150); incubate 48 h at 4 °C with gentle shaking.
Rinse retinas four times in 1.8 mL PBS at 21 °C for 15 min each on a flat‑angle shaker.
Add 200 µL blocking buffer containing the secondary fluorophore‑conjugated antibody (desired concentration) and Streptavidin‑Alexa Fluor 488 (1:200); incubate 48 h at 4 °C with gentle shaking.
CRITICAL: Vortex the antibody‑probe mixture thoroughly, then centrifuge 20 min at 9800 × g (21 °C) to precipitate aggregates; use the supernatant for incubation.
Wash retinas four times in 1.8 mL PBS at 21 °C for 15 min each on a flat‑angle shaker.

description: In contrast to its human counterpart, the development of the mouse retinal vasculature is a post-natal process. In mouse pups, an incipient vascular plexus outgrows from the optic nerve head around birth and gives rise to the superficial vessel layer within the first week (∼P7). These immature vessels undergo extensive rearrangements to mature into a fully functional vessel bed, whilst expanding towards inner layers of the retina, where the deeper (∼P8 to ∼P12) and intermediate (∼P14 to P21) vessel layers are formed.1 Due to easy access, this model has been widely used in studies uncovering the expression of genes encoding key modulators of vascular biology. Such discoveries have been aided by RNA in situ hybridization (ISH)-based methods, either in whole-mount or sectioned retinas. However, the spatial resolution of the detected RNAs is limited due to signal amplification steps or diffusion of the detection reagents.2,3 By allowing the detection of individual transcripts, as well as precise quantification of their numbers, single-molecule fluorescence ISH (smFISH) is hailed as a transformative addition to the toolkit of RNA detection methodologies. smFISH entails sets of 25 to 50 oligonucleotide probes, each 18 to 22 nucleotides long. The probes are individually labeled with a fluorophore and target distinct regions of the transcripts of interest, allowing their detection with great selectivity and sensitivity.4 Despite the successful application of smFISH to the imaging of RNAs in mouse embryonic tissues,5 its use in more complex samples such as whole-mount post-natal retinas has remained challenging. Here, we detail a robust protocol for the detection of single mRNAs, with high spatial resolution, in post-natal retinal vasculature. Although this protocol uses two mRNA species as testbeds, it may be employed to detect other transcripts.
